Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the window again this year.

Seven years ago this month, my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on this tree I could hardly write it. This year I wrote it at the counter, between customers, with the same pen I always use. I'm not telling you that to make it about me. I'm telling you because I think plenty of you know exactly what a small cardboard tag and a pen can do to a person.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, whether or not the person they are missing was cared for by the hospice. You don't need any connection to us at all. If a name matters to you, it belongs on the tree. It doesn't matter how long ago it was, or where they died.

Memory tags will be on the counter from Monday 16 November. There's a suggested donation of £3, which goes to the hospice, and envelopes on the counter too if you'd rather take a tag home and write it in your own time. The tree goes into the window on Saturday 21 November, and we switch the lights on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is doing mince pies again. Do come early if you want one. They have a history of disappearing during the first carol.

Every name on every tag will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don't have to come to the service for your name to be read. We keep every tag afterwards, and they go back to the hospice for safekeeping.

And you don't have to buy anything. You can just come in and stand by the tree for as long as you like. That's what it's there for, and nobody will ask you for anything else. If you want the stool by the window for a while, that's allowed too.

Last year the tree carried 412 names. Thank you to everyone who wrote one, and to everyone who came in just to stand and look, and to those who told us who they were remembering. It means a great deal to us in the shop.

Jean
